paper.title_en: AT 2023rcq: A Nuclear Flare in Coincidence with a High-energy Neutrino
paper.abstract_en: We analyze the photometric and spectroscopic data for AT 2023rcq, a transient flare hosted in the quasar SDSS J014926.13+074311.1 at redshift z = 0.539. The flare appeared to have optical light curves of a tidal disruption event (TDE) type, i.e., a fast rise followed with a slow decay, and was accompanied with a delayed mid-infrared (MIR) flare. More interestingly, a high-energy (HE) neutrino event IC-240327A was found to be detected at the time of the MIR flare. Such temporal and positional coincidence cases have been found for TDEs and the nuclear accretion flares with strong accompanying MIR flares, suggesting TDEs and the accretion flares as potential HE-neutrino emitters. We determine the properties of AT 2023rcq. Based on the results from the light-curve fitting and spectral analysis, in which an optical spectrum obtained by us during the flare is used, AT 2023rcq is likely not a TDE. Also the strength of its MIR flare is relatively weak compared to the sample of the nuclear accretion flares. We discuss AT 2023rcq as a case that may represent a sample of similar properties. Investigations to build such a sample and their possible association with HE neutrinos are warranted.
